rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The summary reports four identified bias occurrences, one each for anchoring effect, availability heuristic, confirmation bias, and groupthink; the detailed identified_occurrences array contains the same four occurrences.

evaluation_limitations: The supplied frozen segment map contains six eligible positive segments and no eligible negative segments; false-alarm and correct-rejection rates therefore have undefined denominators.
No retrieved corpus passages or retrieval logs were supplied, so corpus fidelity cannot be scored.
Attributions to committee members other than the participant are based on retrospective interview evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Two members returned from a regional math conference enthusiastic about Curriculum B; the first working session centered on B and A and C received a checklist pass.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Curriculum B received priority attention because of another district's positive reception, even though the committee had twelve weeks and no scheduling reason to skip an even initial review.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Around scoring, Curriculum A was found to have a stronger differentiated-instruction plan, but discussion remained framed as whether A was good enough to make the committee reconsider B.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Curriculum B remained the implicit reference point for judging A after the initial shortlisting, despite the extended timeline.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: At the vendor meeting, a vivid struggling-classroom turnaround story was remembered clearly while the statistical report covering multiple schools was barely registered and retrieved only weeks later.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The concrete anecdote was more readily recalled and weighted than the less vivid statistical report, despite ample time for prompt retrieval.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The testimonials felt like confirmation of what the committee already believed; the report was treated as something to get to eventually even though nothing prevented retrieving it that week.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Evidence consistent with the favorable view of B was accepted with less scrutiny while potentially complicating evidence was deprioritized.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: A pilot teacher flagged pacing problems; the concern was acknowledged and the conversation moved toward agreement, no second classroom was observed, and one member later said reservations were not voiced because of how the room felt.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The group moved toward apparent consensus without fully airing or investigating dissent, although several weeks remained.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Curriculum A had two very high and two very low differentiation scores; the scores were averaged directly into a settled middling composite without discussing the split, and later it emerged that reviewers had read different appendices.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A wide disagreement was collapsed into a single mean without investigating the underlying divergence despite no urgent deadline.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The finding is correctly localized and fully describes the external-enthusiasm mechanism, but anchoring effect is a distinct label from the hidden Bandwagon effect.

The candidate correctly notices a settled average masking divergent scores, but it proposes a speculative anchoring mechanism rather than the hidden Averaging Bias mechanism and remains explicitly insufficiently evidenced.

candidates.details: The candidate flags a real aggregation concern and correctly withholds definitive identification because routine averaging remains a plausible non-bias explanation. It is useful as a cautious lead, but it does not provide the full Averaging Bias mechanism and cannot become a true positive.

high_only.detection_interpretation: Three of six positive segments are detected by high-confidence identified findings; the moderate Groupthink finding is excluded and no negative segments are available for false-alarm assessment.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Four of six positive segments are detected after adding moderate-confidence findings; the later anchoring and averaging segments remain undetected.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: No low-confidence identified findings are present, so this threshold is numerically identical to high_and_moderate.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: The candidate adds a segment-level detection for the averaging episode, leaving only the later anchoring segment missed; it does not produce an instance-level true positive.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: The identified occurrence fully captures the hidden external-enthusiasm mechanism but assigns it the distinct anchoring label.
The candidate is correctly located and notices an average masking divergent scores, but its proposed anchoring mechanism only partially overlaps the hidden averaging mechanism.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly states that analysis used the transcript alone and that no retrieved corpus passages were supplied. This is appropriately disclosed, and corpus support does not affect the primary detection scores.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Adding the moderate Groupthink finding raises segment hits from 3 to 4 and strict/mechanism-first instance true positives from 2/3 to 4/4.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: No change; there are no low-confidence identified findings.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: The candidate raises segment hits from 4 to 5 but adds no instance-level true positive and adds one false positive to each instance scorecard.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, 4 of 6 positive reasoning segments are detected; the supplied map has no negative segments for false-alarm assessment.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, 4 true positives, 2 false negatives, and 1 false positive yield precision 0.8000, recall 0.6667, and F1 0.7273.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, 4 true positives, 2 false negatives, and 0 false positives yield precision 1.0000, recall 0.6667, and F1 0.8000; the higher score credits the correctly described Bandwagon mechanism despite its wrong label.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The candidate is a useful cautious abstention: it points to a real aggregation concern and adds a segment detection, but it is not sufficiently specific or evidenced to count as an Averaging Bias instance.
main_failure_modes: Missed the distinct later Anchoring Bias instance.
Missed Averaging Bias as an identified occurrence.
Assigned the initial external-enthusiasm mechanism the near-neighbor label anchoring effect instead of Bandwagon effect.
Candidate inclusion adds a false positive at the fourth threshold without improving instance-level recall.
main_strengths: Correctly identified Availability Bias, Confirmation bias, and Groupthink with valid localized evidence.
Correctly captured the Bandwagon mechanism even though the label was wrong.
Explicitly disclosed that no retrieved corpus support was available.
Used a cautious candidate status for the ambiguous aggregation episode rather than overstating certainty.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The run shows strong evidence fidelity and clean precision among identified findings at the recommended threshold, but incomplete coverage of the six-instance hidden manifest. Mechanism-first scoring reveals a taxonomy error for the initial social-endorsement mechanism, while the candidate tier improves segment coverage at the cost of instance-level false positives.
